title: Governance Reviews and Supervisory Interviews: Preparing Your Board and Management
summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors assess governance and interview directors and staff, and how licensees can evidence effective governance and prepare openly.
intro: This training programme equips boards, senior managers and control function holders to understand how supervisors assess governance, to evidence effective oversight, and to take part in supervisory interviews openly and effectively.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To show licensees how a supervisory governance assessment works, from desk review of board packs to interviews with directors and key staff, so that they can strengthen and evidence their governance. Participants leave knowing what supervisors look for in the board, senior management, risk architecture and internal audit, and how to prepare for interviews without scripting or over-coaching.
sections.What It Covers: How supervisors assess governance, the governance pillars, board packs and board dynamics, decision-making and challenge, the role of interviews in supervision, and preparing for and taking part in supervisory interviews.
Intended Audience: Chairs, executive and non-executive directors likely to be interviewed by the supervisor
Senior managers and control function holders in risk, compliance and internal audit
Company secretaries and governance staff who prepare board packs and coordinate supervisory visits
Learning Objectives: Explain how supervisors assess governance and what evidence they use
Assess the firm's governance against the four pillars of board, senior management, risk architecture and internal audit
Evaluate board packs and minutes as a supervisor would read them
Demonstrate effective board challenge and decision-making with evidence
Prepare directors and staff for supervisory interviews openly and appropriately
Respond to interview follow-up and governance findings constructively
sections.Structure and Format: Six modules of about one hour each, delivered as a one-day workshop in person, virtually or in a hybrid format. It combines short briefings with a board pack review case study and interview practice. It can be delivered on its own or with the companion workshops on business models and on supervisory findings and remediation.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of board or senior management work in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of supervisory interviews is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)

modules.title: How Supervisors Assess Governance
modules.summary: Why governance is a core supervisory risk, how a governance assessment is scoped and carried out, and how its conclusions affect the firm's ratings and supervisory engagement.
objectives: Explain the purpose of a supervisory governance assessment
Describe the stages from desk review to conclusions
Anticipate how governance findings are rated and followed up
syllabus: Governance risk and why supervisors assess it
Proportionality and materiality in governance reviews
Desk analysis, interviews and conclusions
What strong, adequate and weak governance look like

modules.title: The Four Pillars of Governance
modules.summary: What supervisors expect from the board, senior management, the risk architecture and internal audit, and how these pillars work together, including over outsourced activities.
objectives: Assess the firm against each governance pillar
Identify gaps between documented and actual governance
Evidence oversight of outsourced and technology services
syllabus: The board: composition, skills, committees and oversight
Senior management and effective delegation
Risk architecture: strategy, risk appetite, risk function and three lines
Internal audit, outsourcing and what the board still owns

modules.title: Board Packs, Board Dynamics and Decision-Making
modules.summary: What the board pack and minutes reveal to a supervisor, and how agendas, chairing, culture and challenge shape the quality of board decisions.
objectives: Apply five tests to the firm's own board pack
Recognise the behavioural red flags supervisors look for
Evidence the quality of a major board decision
syllabus: Reading a board pack: what it shows and what it leaves out
Agenda, chairing, information quality and psychological safety
Groupthink, dominant personalities and information asymmetry
Case study: board pack review

modules.title: The Role of Interviews in Supervision
modules.summary: Why supervisors interview directors and staff, who they interview, how they plan and triangulate evidence, and how they judge credibility and consistency.
objectives: Explain how interviews test documentary evidence
Describe how supervisors plan and sequence interviews
Recognise how answers are assessed for credibility
syllabus: Documents tell supervisors what; interviews test how and why
Who is interviewed and what each perspective reveals
Question types, probing and follow-up
Credibility, consistency and corroboration

modules.title: Preparing for and Taking Part in Supervisory Interviews
modules.summary: How to prepare directors and staff for interviews openly and appropriately, answer clearly and accurately, and avoid the pitfalls that undermine credibility.
objectives: Prepare interviewees without scripting or over-coaching
Answer questions directly with evidence and examples
Handle questions outside the interviewee's knowledge honestly
syllabus: Preparing well: knowing the firm, the papers and your role
Answering the question asked, with specific evidence
Avoiding vague, hedged or rehearsed answers
Interview practice: both sides of the table

modules.title: After the Visit: Findings and Follow-Up
modules.summary: How governance findings are communicated, how to respond to them, and how to turn the review into a lasting improvement in governance.
objectives: Agree realistic remediation and evidence its completion
syllabus: Feedback letters and requests for further information
Responding to findings: accuracy, ownership and context
Remediation actions and evidencing closure
Workshop: a governance improvement plan for your firm

related.title: Engaging Effectively with Your Supervisor: How Firms Are Assessed
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how supervisors assess business models, governance and risk, so they can see themselves as the supervisor does and engage with confidence.

related.title: Fit and Proper for Firms: Appointing and Assessing Key Function Holders
related.summary: A nine-module programme showing firms how to appoint and assess key function holders, prepare applications and interviews, and manage fitness and certification on an ongoing basis.

related.title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms build credible recovery and wind-down plans, from scenarios and triggers to client asset return, testing and supervisory review.

related.title: Regulatory Investigations and Enforcement: Responding as a Firm
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement, from first information request to settlement.

related.title: Regulatory Readiness: Authorisation and Supervisory Engagement
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking firms from licence application through to established supervision, showing how authorities assess applications and supervise new firms.

related.title: Supervisory Findings and Remediation: From Risk Assessment to Closure
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors reach findings and how licensees can respond with remediation that fixes root causes and closes issues on evidence.
